messages.text: The MATS Residency application portal was unavailable for about an hour yesterday, before applications were supposed to be closed. We've extended the application window until at least 3:30 PST today. <https://forms.matsprogram.org/residency-w27?utm_source=generator-residency-eoi&utm_medium=newsletter&utm_campaign=a26|Applications available here>.

Expressions of interest to mentor for *MATS Summer 2027* are open until *Friday, November 6*! If you work in AI alignment, governance, security, or biosecurity and are open to mentoring fellows, please <https://dashboard.matsprogram.org/open/forms/mentor_expression_of_interest?utm_source=slack&utm_medium=slack&utm_campaign=summer27_mentor_eoi|let us know here>.

Mentoring means choosing fellows to work with you around February–March (we help with this), supervising them for 12 weeks from June through August 2027, and, if they do well, possibly continuing with them through a 6–12 month extension.

Fellows you take on are fully supported: a $6,400/month stipend, up to $8,000–$16,000/month in compute, housing, a dedicated research manager, and office space in Berkeley or London. MATS has supported 600+ researchers to date.

If you have any questions about mentoring with MATS, feel free to DM me!

Some Far labs (paid) fun!

> *Paid study ($200): test a new harness for agentic AI safety research* :microscope:
> Hi all! My AI safety research team and I are testing an unreleased harness built for agentic AI safety research, and we’re looking for researchers to try it out. The threshold for participation is not high! You have a good chance of being selected.
> *What it involves:* one 2-hour remote session over video. You’ll step into an agentic research project that’s already in progress, follow along as the agent works, and make the calls at key decision points about where the research goes next. It’s meant to feel a lot like picking up a project midstream with Claude Code or a similar agent. You’ll use it in your browser, with nothing to install.
> *When:* sessions run Nov 9–27.
> *Pay:* $200 for the 2 hour session.
> *You’re a good fit if* you’ve used agents to do AI safety research and have run AI safety and/or control evals.
> Interested? Fill out this short screening form (about 5 minutes): <https://tally.so/r/zEx8V1|tally.so/r/zEx8V1> 
> DM me with any questions or issues and please pass this along to anyone who might be a good fit!
> Thanks, Kaia.

Applications are open for two senior roles in New York’s government that are important for AI safety.

NY’s newly created Office of Digital Innovation, Governance, Integrity, & Trust (DIGIT) will operate as NY’s AI regulator and implement the Responsible Artificial Intelligence Safety & Education (RAISE) Act (one of the most important frontier AI laws enacted in the US). DIGIT is housed within the Department of Financial Services, which is now hiring for two senior roles critical to implementing the RAISE Act:

	*<https://www.dfs.ny.gov/system/files/documents/2026/10/spe_adv_sup_tec_pol_spe_ass_ns_20261030.pdf|Special Advisor to the Superintendent for Technology Policy>*
The Special Advisor will be a senior leader at DFS who helps oversee implementation of the RAISE Act, New York’s frontier AI safety law. Additionally, the Advisor “serves as the subject matter expert and advisor to the Superintendent on technology regulation,” “drives policy and regulatory development,” and “leads executive-level briefings.”

	*<https://www.dfs.ny.gov/system/files/documents/2026/10/sen_cou_tec_pol_spe_ass_ns_20261030.pdf|Senior Counsel for Technology Policy>*
The Senior Counsel will report to the Special Advisor and help oversee implementation of the RAISE Act, New York’s frontier AI safety law. The Counsel will also provide subject matter expertise and offer “strategic counsel on options for policy and regulatory approaches.” They will draft legislation, regulation, and legal opinions, work closely with stakeholders across government, industry, and civil society, and explore “new regulatory tools and approaches.”

The roles are based in NYC. The pay range is $180,562 - $223,625 (salary commensurate with experience), with an additional $4,150 available for an NYC-based appointment. *Applications are due Friday, October 30*.

*Secure AI Project thinks these are important opportunities for folks who want to contribute to frontier AI policy and help ensure that implementation of the RAISE Act goes well.*

If you’re interested in applying, we encourage you to email <mailto:implementation@secureaiproject.org|implementation@secureaiproject.org>, as we can give more context on the roles. Feel free to forward this to candidates you think may be a good fit!

I'm looking for 25+ AI safety/econ/governance/philosophy researchers (PhD students and mats scholars are allowed) to explain one of their recent non-empirical papers or blog posts, and critique an attempt of AI to do the same work, paid $100/hr x 2-3hrs of work. This is to produce an eval set that a frontier lab can use to measure their progress in automating tasks involved in AI risk research. The impact case (I will write more about in an upcoming blog post) is that this dataset will be one of a kind, and can help make the next gen of models better at things we care about, whereas its impact on the automation of research generally is small, given the much larger number of eval sets of that type.

Happy to be reached here or at <mailto:ryan.carey@trajectorylabs.net|ryan.carey@trajectorylabs.net>

*Boston Biosecurity Hackathon, Nov. 15 ($5,000 cash prize, no coding required)*

I’m organizing the in-person *Boston Biosecurity Hackathon* with ASTRAL and CBAI on *Sunday, November 15, in Cambridge*. We’ll explore both ordinary scientific use of AI and adversarial red-teaming through guided challenges on an organizer-provided platform.
We’re especially looking for research assistants, research-experienced students, postdocs, industry scientists, clinicians, and public-health researchers. *$5,000 in cash prizes, with food and AI token costs covered by <https://www.cbai.ai/|CBAI>.*

The resulting dataset supports <https://astral.detection.bio/|CBAI's ASTRAL project> (an open-source scanner for biological-misuse risk in AI logs) and will be made available to qualified biosecurity research groups under a research-use governance framework. It’s a chance to meet local researchers, learn about AI and biosecurity, and contribute research conversations to the ASTRAL project. Data-use and retention terms will be shared before participation.

*Details and application:* <https://luma.com/0iufmn6q|luma.com/…>
*Questions:* ASTRAL@detection.bio
